title: Relative oral bioavailability and tolerability of hydrocortisone from 2-dimensionally printed orodispersible films in children and adolescents with primary adrenal insufficiency (REPLACE trial)
official: Relative oral bioavailability and tolerability of hydrocortisone from 2-dimensionally printed orodispersible films in children and adolescents with primary adrenal insufficiency (REPLACE trial)
summary: Main objective: To investigate the relative bioavailability (F) of orally administered hydrocortisone ODF compared to hydrocortisone oral tablets in children and adolescents with primary adrenal insufficiency.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Participants meeting all of the following criteria will be considered for enrolment into the clinical trial: Written, personally signed and dated informed consent (by legal representatives) as well as pediatric assent (from participants, where appropriate) to participate in the trial prior to any trial-related interventions, in accordance with the International Conference on Harmo-nisation (ICH) GCP Guideline E6, and applicable regulations (CTR).
2. A female of childbearing potential is defined as a female capable of becoming pregnant, which includes participants who have had their first menstrual cycle (i.e., menarche) and are not surgically sterile (i.e., bilateral oophorectomy, hysterectomy, or bilateral tubal liga-tion for at least 3 months prior to screening) (see Appendix 3 for detailed contraceptive guidance). A man is considered fertile after puberty unless permanently sterile by bilateral orchidectomy. Male participants and their partners must use highly effective methods of contraception (i. e, condom in male subjects and highly effective contraception in their female partners) trough and continue to use contraception and refrain from fathering a child for up to one week after the last IMP.
3. Willingness to adhere to pandemic regulations should they be issued during the trial, and
4. Consent to comply with specified lifestyle and dietary requirements (see section 4.5).
5. Be a female or male of 7 to 17 y inclusive at the time of signed informed consent/assent.
6. Medically confirmed diagnosis of primary adrenal insufficiency (classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency and non-classical CAH forms based on standard medically accepted criteria and genetically confirmed, and autoimmune pri-mary adrenal insufficiency, requiring chronic corticosteroid replacement therapy).
7. Stable hydrocortisone substitution for ≥ 2 weeks prior to screening and V1.
8. If treated with fludrocortisone, the dose should be stable for at least 1 month prior to screening. Independent of fludrocortisone administration, the upright plasma renin activity (PRA) during screening (in the absence of drugs confounding PRA interpretation) should be < 3 x of ULN and > LLN on the participants’ usual sodium intake (if PRA > 2 x of ULN and < 3 x of ULN, participants must have normal age-specific systolic blood pressure and heart rate and serum potassium 
9. ACTH should be < 2 x ULN.
10. 17-OHP and androstenedione should be within the individually appropriate levels based on the discretion of the investigator (of the attending pediatric endocrinologist).
11. Understanding, ability, and willingness to fully comply with trial interventions and re-strictions.
12. If of reproductive/childbearing potential and sexually active, female and male participants must agree to use a highly effective method of contraception throughout the trial and up to one week after their last IMP administration.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participants presenting with any of the following criteria will not be included in the clinical trial: 1. A person (either participant or legal representatives) who, in the opinion of the investigator, is unwilling or unable to adhere to the requirements of the trial.
2. History of malignancy, unless successfully treated with curative intent and considered to be cured.
3. Diabetes mellitus type 1, 2, or 3 (other specific types of diabetes) according to the ADA criteria [American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee, 2024].
4. Any acute or chronic illness or clinically relevant finding known or expected to modify ab-sorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of hydrocortisone.
5. Any known history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to trial drugs, other drugs, food, or any other clinically significant allergies or hypersensitivity reactions.
6. A positive result in the drug screening test in urine at SCR.
7. Use of an IMP in another clinical trial within 30 d or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to the expected date of receiving the first dose of IMP in the current trial or active enrol-ment in another drug clinical trial.
8. A prior vaccination within < 2 weeks (< 4 weeks in case of live-attenuated vaccines) before the first IMP administration or any urgent plans to get vaccinated during the running trial.
9. A positive human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or hepatitis C (HCV) antibody screen, or a positive result for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).
10. Known hypersensitivity to the ODF or to any of its excipients.
11. Have current substance dependence or substance or alcohol abuse (e.g., more than 12 g / d in females und more than 24 g / d in males on average) or expected noncompliance to refrain from alcohol 24 h before the PK days.
12. A person (either participant or legal representatives) who is an employee of the Investiga-tor or sponsor or study site, with direct involvement in the proposed study or other studies under the direction of that Investigator or study site, as well as family members of the employees or the Investigator.
13. Unable to refrain from smoking during trial days.
14. Relevant change of co-medication within two weeks prior to planned V1, especially new or changed intake of inhibitors or inducers of cytochrome P450 (CYP) isozymes.
15. Have had a blood loss ≥ 3% of total blood volume (based on 75 mL per kg body weight) within 8 weeks before Day 1.
16. relevant findings in any of the following investigations at SCR (minor deviations of laboratory values from the normal range can be acceptable, if judged by the investigator to be of no clinical relevance for this trial): a. Hb < 11 g/dL (males and females) b. White blood cell (WBC) count < 4.0 × 103/mm3 c. Platelet count < 100,000/mm3 d. Absolute neutrophil count <1.0 × 103/mm3 e. Estimated GFR (using modified Schwartz formula for ages 12 to 17 years) ≤ 60 ml/min/1.73 m2 f. Total bilirubin > 1.5 x ULN unless due to a documented diagnosis of Gilbert’s syn-drome g. ALT > 2 x ULN h. AST > 2 x ULN i. CK not within normal limits (participants with CK elevations between 1.5 - 3 x ULN may be included if troponin T is negative) j. Serum sodium < 132 mmol/L.
17. A person who is institutionalized pursuant to a court order or an order by a government agency or is in residential care institutions.
18. Any medical disorder that may require treatment or make the participant unlikely to fully complete the trial, or any condition that presents undue risk from the IMP or trial interven-tions.
19. Is at increased risk of developing adrenal crisis in the investigator’s opinion, based on, for example, repeated history of adrenal crisis in the past, prior history of adrenal crisis pre-cipitated by reducing glucocorticoid dose, recent episode(s), etc.
20. Pregnancy or breast feeding.
21. Late onset congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
22. Secondary adrenal insufficiency.
23. Treatment with other glucocorticoids (e.g. prednisolone, dexamethasone) or modified-re-lease hydrocortisone preparations (e.g. Efmody®).
